title: AMSTAR 2: A critical appraisal tool for systematic reviews that include randomised or non-randomised studies of healthcare interventions, or both

extracted.subtask_short: Judging whether review conclusions are trustworthy
extracted.subtask_description: Determines whether a systematic review's stated conclusions can be trusted, by separating methodological flaws into critical vs non-critical domains and combining them via an explicit algorithm into an overall confidence verdict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical vs non-critical methodological flaw domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Separates 16 checklist items into 7 'critical' domains (protocol registration, literature search adequacy, justification for exclusions, risk-of-bias assessment adequacy, meta-analytic method appropriateness, whether risk of bias was accounted for in interpretation, publication bias assessment) that fundamentally threaten conclusion validity if failed, vs 9 'non-critical' items whose absence degrades quality but does not on its own invalidate conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMSTAR 2 authors explicitly note reviewers should feel free to prespecify their own critical-item set appropriate to the review topic if the default seven do not fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-tier overall confidence rating algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: High: no or one non-critical weakness - review provides an accurate and comprehensive summary. Moderate: more than one non-critical weakness but no critical flaws - review may provide an accurate summary. Low: one critical flaw, with or without non-critical weaknesses - review may not provide an accurate and comprehensive summary. Critically low: more than one critical flaw - review should not be relied on to provide an accurate and comprehensive summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple non-critical weaknesses can also justify a discretionary downgrade from moderate to low even absent a critical flaw. No numeric summary score should ever be calculated from the 16 items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forced Yes/Partial Yes/No response categories, no benefit of doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: Items are rated 'Yes,' 'Partial Yes,' or 'No.' The authors deliberately removed 'not applicable' and 'cannot answer' options to force a judgment; where information is simply unavailable in the report, the rater should assign 'No' rather than giving the benefit of the doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias must be reflected in interpretation confidence (item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit reference to the risk-of-bias findings when drawing the review's conclusions and making recommendations - the claim's confidence language must actually reflect the quality of the underlying studies, not just their number or direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of risk-of-bias assessment method (item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment must cover the bias domains specified in validated instruments (e.g., Cochrane RoB tools) - baseline confounding, selection bias, measurement bias, selective outcome reporting - with appropriate, separate tools used for randomized vs. non-randomized designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of literature search strategy (item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search across multiple relevant databases, with particular attention to whether non-randomized/grey literature sources were also searched where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for excluding individual studies (item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A full accounting of excluded studies with transparent, study-by-study or category-level reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of meta-analytic pooling methods (item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: An explicit, protocol-level statement of the decision rules for whether/how to pool studies, including judgment of clinical and methodological compatibility before pooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication bias assessment and impact discussion (item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of statistical tests or graphical displays (e.g., funnel plot) with discussion of likely impact on the conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper notes a practical constraint that funnel-plot asymmetry tests are unreliable with fewer than ~10 studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process failures that sever claim from cited evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A review's stated conclusion can fail to be well-supported for process reasons entirely separate from whether individual included studies were high quality: an incomplete search (item 4), unaccounted risk of bias (items 9/13), inappropriate pooling (item 11), or undetected publication bias (item 15) can each independently sever the link between 'what the cited studies show' and 'what the review claims they show.'
